mechanism_narrative: A higher federal funds rate compresses equity valuations by increasing discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This mechanism is active during monetary tightening cycles.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is above 5.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals labor market deterioration, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: Rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) combined with a stable or rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals persistent inflationary pressures and monetary tightening expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (CPIAUCSL rising and FEDFUNDS stable or rising) fails to predict negative returns in > 40% of cases (Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: During a housing market downturn (HOUST declining), S&P 500 returns are negative over the next 60 days due to the housing sector's drag on the broader economy.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST is declining.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a weakening manufacturing sector, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO decline fails to predict negative returns in > 40% of cases (Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-year window).

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales (RSAFS) indicate strong consumer spending, boosting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS rise fails to predict positive returns in > 40% of cases (Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-year window).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 5.0%, it signals an active monetary tightening cycle, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment growth (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in PAYEMS and HOUST fails to predict negative returns in > 40% of cases (Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-year window).
